items.prompt: Which word means full of colour?

options.why: Colourless means without colour. The ending -less means without.
Colourly is not a word.
Colours means more than one colour.

hints: Look at the end of each word.
Which ending means full of?
Cross out the words you know are wrong, like colours. Then compare the endings left.
items.explanation: The suffix -ful means full of, so colourful means full of colour.

options.why: Fearful means full of fear. That is the opposite!
Feared is a past verb, as in people feared the storm.
Fearly is not a word.

hints: Which ending means without?
-ful means full of. Another ending means without.
Cover fear in each word and look only at the endings.
items.explanation: The suffix -less means without, so fearless means without fear.

items.prompt:
Add -ful or -less to care.
The glass broke into pieces. Be ___ when you pick them up!
hints: Broken glass is sharp.
Do you want to be full of care, or without care?
Write care, then add the ending you chose. Check how many l letters it has.
items.explanation: Careful means full of care. When you pick up broken glass, you must be careful.

options.why: The suffix -ful has only one l.
Keep the e from hope: hope + ful.
Hopefuly is not a word. The y is not needed here.

hints: The word is made from hope and an ending.
Do not change hope. Check how many l letters the ending has.
Write hope first, then add the ending carefully.
items.explanation: Hope + ful = hopeful. The suffix -ful always has just one l.

items.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.
hints: Look at the ending of each word.
-ful means full of, -less means without, and -ly tells how.
Start with slowly. Which meaning tells how something is done?
items.explanation: The ending -ful means full of, -less means without, and -ly tells us how. So painful is full of pain, and slowly is in a slow way.

items.prompt:
Add -ly to happy.
The children sang ___ in the sunshine.
hints: Happy ends in a consonant and then y.
When a word ends in a consonant and y, the y changes before you add -ly.
Write happ, then think: which letter takes the place of y?
items.explanation: Happy ends in y after a consonant, so the y changes to i. Happy + ly = happily.

items.prompt: Add -ly to gentle. Which spelling is right?

options.why: For words ending in -le, the -le changes to -ly.
This adds a y, but the e must go too.
There is no i in this word.

hints: Gentle ends in -le.
For words that end in -le, you swap the -le for -ly.
Look at simple and simply. Do the same with gentle.
items.explanation: When a word ends in -le, change the -le to -ly. Gentle becomes gently, just like simple becomes simply.

items.prompt: Sort the words by what the ending means.
hints: Look at the last few letters of each word.
-ful means full of, and -less means without.
Start with joyful. Does it end in -ful or -less?
items.explanation: Words ending in -ful mean full of something, like joyful. Words ending in -less mean without something, like spotless.

items.prompt: There was not one cloud in the sky. The sky was ___.

options.why: Cloudy means there are clouds in the sky.
Cloudful is not a word.
Cloudly is not a word.

hints: How many clouds were in the sky?
You need a word that means without clouds.
Which ending means without?
items.explanation: The ending -less means without. A cloudless sky has no clouds at all.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses the right word?

options.why: This needs -ly at the end to tell how the baby slept.
Peaceless is not a word, and it does not tell how.
Peacely is not a word. Add -ful first, then -ly.

hints: The missing word tells us how the baby slept.
Start with peace, add -ful, then add -ly.
When -ful and -ly join, how many l letters will there be?
items.explanation: Peace + ful = peaceful, and peaceful + ly = peacefully. There is a double l where -ful and -ly join.

items.prompt:
Add -ful and then -ly to care.
Pour the hot tea ___.
hints: Hot tea can spill and burn.
First make care into a -ful word. Then add -ly.
After you add -ful, there is one l. What happens when -ly joins it?
items.explanation: Care + ful = careful, then careful + ly = carefully. The finished word has a double l.

items.prompt: Add -ful to beauty. Which spelling is right?

options.why: When a word ends in a consonant and y, the y changes to i first.
Close! But -ful has only one l.
Do not drop the y. Change it to i.

hints: Beauty ends in a consonant and then y.
Think about how happy changes when you add -ly.
Write beaut, then decide which letter takes the place of y.
items.explanation: Beauty ends in t and then y, so the y changes to i. Beauty + ful = beautiful, with one l.
